Analysis.object: Sport pressures and dietary restraint were highly stable over the course of a competitive season. Pressures gymnasts and swimmers/divers experienced regarding body weight, size, and appearance from their coaches and teammates predicted decreases in their body satisfaction over a 5-month period; this change occurred even though the athletes’ body mass index did not change significantly over that time.

Included only NCAA Division I Female gymnasts and swimmers/divers, who also happened to primarily be Caucasien. The authors examined the variables over only a 5-month period, which represented one competitive collegiate season for these athletes. They examined the relationships among only sport pressures, body dissatisfaction and dietary restraint, additional research is needed to examine other variables such as general sociatail pressures, internalization, and negative affect. The validity of self-report measures of dietary restraint as predictors of actual reductions in food intake has been challenged. Self report measures of dietary restraint are risk factors in the prediction of disordered eating attitudes and behaviors, the measures are poor predictors of behaviorally observed, acute dietary restriction. BMI did not vary over the course of the 5-month season, we were not able to obtain more sensitive measures of body composition due to the study's design.

Health care personnel can help coaches and teammates become more aware of how, through their behaviors and comments, they create an environment that pressures athletes about their body, weight, and appearance. Sport health care professionals can target sport administrators and sport-governing bodies because they have the power to male policy changes that can improve the sport environment, maling it less toxic for athletes. Such entities, could make revealing uniforms less so, adjust judging criteria so there is less focus on aesthetic/appearance-based aspects of the performance, expand or raise weight classifications, and/or set up strict requirements regarding acceptable weight loss over specific periods of time. Preventive programming, sport health care profesionals can work directly with athletes to help them counter these sport pressures and reduce their likelihood of engaging in caloric restriction of feeling dissatisfied with their bodies. 
Future reseach should examine whether our findings are supported in other groups of Female athletes (e.g., different sports, different competitive levels, more diverse racial/ethnic groups); male athletes should also be studied and such research should include measures of drive for muscularity. Other longitudinal studies may want to examine eating disorders and other potential risk factors over a longer period of time, or a different period (e.g., from the end of the competitive season to the start of the next one).
